newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian share index falls further in weak market.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian share index falls further in weak market.

text.p: Bearish tendencies persisted on the Nigerian stock market on Tuesday, forcing the all-share index to close lower for the second day running, dealers said.
The index closed at 7798.32 from 7933.63 on Monday.
Dealers said there was no end in sight to factors weighing down the market.
"There is yet no significant injection of funds into the economy which the market is looking up to to end this current trend," one said.
A combination of economic factors and perceived overvaluation of share prices have caused a sell-off of many blue chips.
Leading market losers on Tuesday included Coca-Cola bottler, the Nigerian Bottling Company, which fell 50 kobo to 46.40 naira and oil marketer Unipetrol, which closed 40 kobo lower at 59.60 naira.
Others were African Petroleum at 46.00 naira, NCR at 12.70 naira and United Bank for Africa at 11.70 naira, all 30 kobo weaker.
Dunlop ended 42 kobo down at 8.08 naira and conglomerate Lever Brothers fell 20 kobo to 21.40 naira.
Gains were restricted to a few banking and insurance firms.
Afribank climbed five kobo to 4.17 naira and Owena Bank rose one kobo to 1.51 naira.
Niger Insurance advanced 10 kobo to 2.85 naira while newly-listed Cornerstone Insurance ended five stronger at 2.75 naira.
